messages:
Ravi: Quick sync about the compact-header handshake proposal for telemetry ingress - we need a concrete default before next week's rollout.
Maya: Reminder of options: full-ingest, strip-and-breadcrumb, or sidecar-canonicalize.
Tess: Full-ingest = simplest for queries but kills storage/cost. Sidecar canonicalize delays pain but is operationally heavy.
Ravi: Strip-and-breadcrumb attempts middle ground: drop non-whitelisted attrs, attach a tiny header with (origin,sdk,compat_v,attr_signature).
Irene: How does attribution work if we drop fields? Can we rely on the signature to rehydrate later?
Tess: Signature only points to a revive record in a short-term store; we keep sampled full-payloads forever for audits.
Maya: Numbers from bench: strip-and-breadcrumb halves payload bloat vs full-ingest and saves ~7% CPU vs sidecar.
Irene: Risk: developer debugs that need missing fields will be painful. Need a clear developer support flow + sampling policy.
Ravi: Proposed default: adopt strip-and-breadcrumb, 72-hour revive window for full payload rehydration, sampled full retention at 0.5% by default, tenant override supported.
Maya: +1, but require SDK owners to set compat_v before pruning; DevEx to send migration notice.
Tess: Ops: will add a revive cache and a small bump in TTL-tier capacity.
ops-bot: /remind #eng-platform in 3 days to review ingress telemetry rollout checklist. :bell:
Irene: I'll draft the playbook for debugging and audit fallbacks.
Ravi: Thanks everyone — landing decision here and will update the RFC doc.
